$comment: Source of truth for terrain types. Every hex's `terrain` is one of these ids.
ADDING A TYPE: add an entry here, then add its row to the terrain table in
data/maps/README.md. tools/map-viewer/terrain.test.js asserts the two agree, and
tools/map-import.ts refuses a terrain value that is not declared here, so a typo
and a genuinely new type can no longer look alike.
`surface` is the intrinsic land/water classification the README's arctic-sea rule and
the lake-vs-ocean flood fill already depend on. It is a property of the landform.
TRAVEL COST AND DIFFICULTY ARE DELIBERATELY ABSENT. doc/adr/005 classifies what the
rules let a character do somewhere as app-owned campaign configuration rather than
world data, so travel rules key off the ids here from the application side. Adding a
difficulty column to this file would put a rules number in a world-data record.
This registry is contract-shaped: the KB needs the same vocabulary for the
terrain-change fact type doc/adr/005 calls for. It moves to packages/contract when
issue #7 lands. Until then the data layer is the one place both the zero-dependency
browser viewer and the Node tooling can read it without a build step.
Colours are mimetic - water blue, forest green - so the map reads as a map, not as a
categorical chart. New colours are measured against the existing set rather than
eyeballed; see the terrain section of data/maps/README.md for the current margins.
